title: UPSC CSE Prelims 2026 Conducted Today - 8.19 Lakh Appeared, Answer Key Soon, Result in June
author: Ash K.
summary: UPSC Civil Services Preliminary Examination 2026 held on May 24 across India. Over 8.19 lakh candidates appeared in two shifts. GS Paper 1 from 9:30 AM–11:30 AM, CSAT Paper 2 from 2:30 PM–4:30 PM. 933 vacancies. Provisional answer key expected by May 31. Result expected mid-June to mid-July 2026.
body: The UPSC Civil Services Examination (CSE) Prelims 2026 was conducted today, May 24, 2026 (Sunday), at exam centres across India. Over 8.19 lakh candidates appeared for this year's exam - the first stage of the selection process for IAS, IPS, IFS, and other central services.

DetailInformation
Exam DateMay 24, 2026 (Sunday)
Candidates Appeared8.19 lakh+
GS Paper 1 Timing9:30 AM – 11:30 AM
CSAT Paper 2 Timing2:30 PM – 4:30 PM
Total Vacancies (2026 cycle)933 posts
GS Paper 1 Marks200 marks (100 MCQs, 2 marks each)
CSAT Paper 2 (qualifying)200 marks - minimum 33% required
Negative Marking1/3 mark deducted per wrong answer
Provisional Answer KeyExpected - candidates can challenge by May 31
Prelims Result ExpectedMid-June to early July 2026 (based on past trends)
Mains Exam DateAugust 21, 2026
Expected Cutoff (General)~85 marks (estimated, based on past trends)

What happened today: The exam was conducted in two sessions. GS Paper 1 (General Studies) from 9:30 AM to 11:30 AM determined qualifying marks. CSAT Paper 2 (Civil Services Aptitude Test) from 2:30 PM to 4:30 PM is qualifying in nature - candidates must score minimum 33% (66 out of 200). Candidates needed to arrive at least 30 minutes before exam start and carry their admit card and photo ID.

Provisional answer key: Coaching institutes including Vajiram & Ravi and Legacy IAS have released unofficial answer keys. The official provisional answer key from UPSC will be released on upsconline.nic.in. Candidates can challenge the provisional answer key online via the QPRep portal by May 31 till 6:00 PM. Each challenge must be backed with proof and is subject to a fee.

Expected cutoff 2026: Based on past trends and vacancy count - the 2025 General category cutoff was 92.66 marks. With 933 vacancies in 2026 (slightly fewer than 2025), and depending on paper difficulty, the expected General category cutoff is estimated at approximately 85 marks or slightly higher. Candidates scoring 80 and above should begin Mains preparation without waiting for the official result.

What happens next: UPSC will release the official Prelims Result 2026 typically 15–20 days after the exam, putting it in mid-June to early July 2026. Shortlisted candidates will then appear for Mains, starting August 21, 2026. The result comes as a PDF with roll numbers - no scores are disclosed. Approximately 12–13 times the number of vacancies are shortlisted for Mains.
Check our complete UPSC CSE exam guide covering full syllabus, strategy, and preparation resources. Also see NDA exam guide for defence service aspirants.

faqs.question: How many candidates appeared for UPSC Prelims 2026?
faqs.answer: Over 8.19 lakh candidates appeared for UPSC CSE Prelims 2026 held on May 24, 2026, across exam centres throughout India.

faqs.question: When will the UPSC Prelims 2026 result be declared?
faqs.answer: Based on past trends, the UPSC Prelims 2026 result is expected in mid-June to early July 2026. In 2025, the result came 17 days after the exam. UPSC does not announce the result date in advance.

faqs.question: What is the expected cutoff for UPSC Prelims 2026?
faqs.answer: The expected General category cutoff is approximately 85 marks based on past trends and the 933 vacancies announced. The 2025 cutoff was 92.66 for General. Final cutoff is announced only after the complete selection process ends.

faqs.question: When can candidates challenge the UPSC 2026 answer key?
faqs.answer: Candidates can challenge the provisional answer key through the QPRep portal at upsconline.nic.in by May 31, 2026 till 6:00 PM.

faqs.question: When is the UPSC Mains 2026 exam?
faqs.answer: UPSC CSE Mains 2026 is scheduled to begin on August 21, 2026. Candidates who clear Prelims 2026 will be eligible to appear for Mains.

faqs.question: Is CSAT Paper 2 qualifying in UPSC Prelims?
faqs.answer: Yes. CSAT (Paper 2) is qualifying in nature. Candidates must score a minimum of 33% (66 out of 200 marks). Only GS Paper 1 marks count for the Prelims merit list.

callout.heading: Scored 80+? Start Mains Prep Now
callout.content: Don't wait for the official Prelims result. If you attempted 85+ questions with reasonable accuracy in GS Paper 1, begin your Mains preparation immediately. UPSC Mains 2026 starts August 21 - you have under 90 days.
